name: cubic ZnS
paper: E. D. Palik and A. Addamiano, "Zinc sulfide (ZnS)", in E. D. Palik (ed.), Handbook of Optical Constants of Solids, Academic Press (1985); as compiled by D. Kitzmann and K. Heng, "Optical properties of potential condensates in exoplanetary atmospheres", Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. 475 (2018) 94–107, DOI 10.1093/mnras/stx3141
source: Kitzmann and Heng 2018's compilation (D. Kitzmann and K. Heng, "Optical properties of potential condensates in exoplanetary atmospheres", Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. 475 (2018) 94–107, DOI 10.1093/mnras/stx3141), LX-MIE's compilation/ZnS.dat at commit 38cc6d97c2268d58c41ccfc3955283ab6ee2ca44, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NewStrangeWorlds/LX-MIE/38cc6d97c2268d58c41ccfc3955283ab6ee2ca44/compilation/ZnS.dat, SHA-256 32607bcb78368bfcbb38a6bef88b03b88277b8644a434dc4385f034bd5c04efa, fetched 2026-10-14; read as data, as the only machine-readable copy of its primary
licence: reduced values from Kitzmann and Heng 2018's compilation, the only machine-readable copy found, cited to the primary and to Kitzmann and Heng as the compiler: the measured values are the authors' facts, and the repository's GPL-3.0 covers its code and arrangement, not a reduced visible subset of one material; its compilation/readme.txt sets no separate terms for the data. No compilation file and none of LX-MIE's code is committed (decision-composition §5; decision-r08-licences.md)
reduction: n linear and k linear in log k in wavelength between the source's rows, onto 380–780 nm every 5 nm, to six significant figures; the source's rows are 354, 382, 413 and 451 nm, then about 8–25 nm apart, and its k falls from 0.04 at 413 nm to 7.4 × 10⁻⁶ at 451 nm, across which it is interpolated in log k. Palik's handbook is closed, so its values are read through the compilation (decision-r08-t5d ruling 5). Its k of 0.04–0.06 at 382–413 nm lies longward of cubic ZnS's band gap, near 340 nm, where Debenham 1984 measured the crystal's n (Appl. Opt. 23, 2238), so it is suspect, perhaps a seam between two data sets; kept as the compilation gives it and recorded. The copy states no temperature
